title: Sturge-Weber Syndrome, Ataxia Telangiectasia and Von Hippel-Lindau Disease

steps.title: Sturge-Weber Syndrome Somatic Pathogenesis

vis.alt: Dermatomal vascular cutaneous capillary malformation distribution and leptomeningeal angioma
vis.caption: Vascular cutaneous malformation in ophthalmic distribution associated with leptomeningeal angiomatosis (StewardMD).

steps.tx: The molecular basis of encephalofacial angiomatosis centers on **Sturge-Weber somatic GNAQ mutation**, specifically a postzygotic mosaic activating variant (c.548G>A, p.Arg183Gln) in GNAQ on chromosome 9q21. Somatic mosaicism in vascular endothelial progenitors disrupts endothelin signaling, resulting in malformed microvascular beds manifesting as facial port-wine stains, ipsilateral leptomeningeal angiomas, and secondary ocular choroidal hemangiomas.
steps.say: Sturge-Weber syndrome is caused by a somatic mosaic activating mutation in the GNAQ gene, resulting in vascular capillary venous malformations.

steps.title: Cerebral Tram-Track Gyriform Calcifications

left.title: Computed Tomography Findings
points: Progressive cortical atrophy ipsilateral to facial nevus
Enlarged choroid plexus with prominent transmedullary veins

right.title: Pathophysiology of Calcification
points: Chronic venous stasis in stagnant leptomeningeal angioma
Tissue ischemia, hypoxia, and secondary laminar necrosis
Progressive calcification of cortical layers II and III

steps.tx: Non-contrast brain computed tomography demonstrates pathognomonic **Tram-track calcification on CT**, visible as parallel serpentine gyriform calcifications along atrophic parieto-occipital gyri. Chronic venous stasis and microvascular thrombosis within the stagnant leptomeningeal angioma cause local cortical ischemia and laminar necrosis, precipitating progressive dystrophic mineralization of underlying cortical gray matter layers II and III.
steps.say: Non-contrast brain CT reveals classic tram-track gyriform calcifications along atrophic cortex, driven by chronic leptomeningeal venous stasis.

steps.title: Ataxia Telangiectasia ATM Gene and Biomarkers

rows: Autosomal recessive null mutations in ATM (11q22.3)
Defective DNA double-strand break repair kinase
Vascular ectasias spreading to sun-exposed ears/neck

steps.tx: Understanding the genetics and laboratory profile of **Ataxia telangiectasia ATM gene and AFP** is essential for prompt pediatric diagnosis. Autosomal recessive mutations in the ATM gene on chromosome 11q22.3 disrupt cellular DNA double-strand break repair. Progressive cerebellar ataxia manifests during early childhood alongside oculocutaneous telangiectasias and markedly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP > 10 ng/mL) in over 95% of affected children.
steps.say: Ataxia telangiectasia is caused by mutations in the ATM DNA repair gene, presenting with progressive cerebellar ataxia and elevated serum alpha fetoprotein.

steps.title: Immunodeficiency and Malignancy Predisposition in AT

left.title: Immunological Deficits
points: Severe deficiency of IgA, IgG2 subclasses, and IgE
Thymic hypoplasia with CD4 and CD8 lymphopenia

right.title: Malignancy & Radiation Vulnerability
points: 100-fold increased risk of lymphoma and leukemia
Carcinomas of breast, stomach, and liver in adults
Extreme cellular sensitivity; ionizing radiation contraindicated

steps.tx: Patients with AT suffer profound consequences from **AT immunodeficiency and malignancy risk**, displaying hypogammaglobulinemia (especially IgA, IgG2, and IgE deficiency) alongside progressive lymphopenia. Recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections cause bronchiectasis and respiratory demise. Impaired DNA break repair drives a 100-fold increase in acute lymphoblastic leukemia and T-cell lymphomas; diagnostic ionizing radiation and radiomimetic chemotherapy are strictly avoided.
steps.say: Severe sinopulmonary immunodeficiency and an extreme risk of lymphoid malignancies define ataxia telangiectasia; diagnostic radiation is strictly contraindicated.

steps.title: Von Hippel-Lindau Tumor Suppressor Genetics

vis.alt: Angiogenesis pathway diagram showing hypoxia inducible factor upregulation and VEGF release
vis.caption: Loss of VHL tumor suppressor prevents HIF degradation, driving constitutive VEGF transcription and vascular tumors (StewardMD).

steps.tx: In autosomal dominant cancer syndromes, **Von Hippel-Lindau VHL gene and hemangioblastomas** is caused by germline inactivating mutations or microdeletions of the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25.3. Loss of the VHL E3 ubiquitin ligase prevents proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha), causing hypervascular tumors: cerebellar and retinal hemangioblastomas, clear-cell renal cell carcinomas, and pheochromocytomas.
steps.say: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is caused by VHL tumor suppressor mutations on chromosome 3p, driving constitutive hypoxia inducible factor signaling and hemangioblastomas.

steps.title: Targeted HIF-2alpha Inhibition with Belzutifan

rows: 120 mg orally once daily in adolescents/adults
Continuous therapy until progression or toxicity
Induces tumor regression, sparing repeated neurosurgery

steps.tx: Therapeutic oncological management has been revolutionized by **Belzutifan therapy in VHL**, an oral small-molecule inhibitor targeting hypoxia-inducible factor 2-alpha. Administered at 120 mg daily, belzutifan blocks HIF-2alpha transcription of angiogenic vascular endothelial growth factors. The agent is regulatory-approved for non-metastatic VHL-associated central nervous system hemangioblastomas, clear-cell renal carcinoma, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, sparing repeated resections.
steps.say: Belzutifan is a breakthrough oral HIF two alpha inhibitor approved at one hundred twenty milligrams daily for VHL associated hemangioblastomas and renal tumors.

steps.title: Incontinentia Pigmenti Evolution and Genetics

nodes.label: Stage 4: Adult atrophic hypopigmented linear scars

steps.tx: In x-linked neurocutaneous syndromes, **Incontinentia pigmenti stages** follow mutations in the IKBKG (NEMO) gene on chromosome Xq28, which is lethal in males. Affected females exhibit 4 distinct cutaneous phases distributing along Blaschko lines: neonatal vesicular pustules with peripheral eosinophilia, infantile verrucous plaques, childhood marble-cake hyperpigmented whorls, and adult atrophic hypopigmented hairless streaks associated with retinal neovascularization and encephalopathy.
steps.say: Incontinentia pigmenti progresses through four classic cutaneous stages along lines of Blaschko, caused by X-linked mutations in the NEMO gene.

steps.title: Sturge-Weber Ocular Surveillance Protocol

left.title: Ophthalmic Risk Factors
points: Port-wine stain involving V1 ophthalmic distribution
Involvement of upper eyelid margins carries highest risk
Congenital or early juvenile glaucoma occurs in 30-70%

right.title: Surveillance & Therapy
points: Monitor corneal diameter, cup-to-disc ratio & buphthalmos
Topical latanoprost and timolol; early goniotomy surgery

steps.tx: Every newborn with an upper facial port-wine stain requires **Port-wine stain eye screening protocol**, because capillary-venous malformations involving the V1 ophthalmic trigeminal dermatome and upper eyelid carry a 30-70% risk of ipsilateral glaucoma. Elevated episcleral venous pressure and trabecular meshwork dysplasia mandate serial intraocular pressure assessments every 3-6 months. Medical therapy with timolol and latanoprost or goniotomy prevents irreversible amblyopic vision loss.
steps.say: Infants with V1 facial port wine stains require serial intraocular pressure checks every three to six months to detect glaucoma and prevent amblyopic blindness.
